Subject: HealthDocs procurement — PO details and invoice cadence

Hi Olga / Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Finance asked me to confirm a few vendor-side billing requirements before we move to final PO issuance:

- PO number must appear on every invoice line and as the invoice reference.
- Our standard terms are Net 90. We typically cannot accept shorter terms without a senior approval exception.
- Invoices must either be issued per contract milestone (with milestone IDs matching the PO line items) or as a consolidated monthly statement (we prefer consolidated monthly where possible).
- For milestone invoicing, each invoice needs the milestone ID and deliverable description to match the PO.
- We require vendor tax paperwork (W-9) and a signed SOW prior to first payment.

Attached: SOW_HealthDocs_v3.pdf — this is the internal SOW draft we expect to match line items on the PO (happy to review redlines).

One additional ask: because this is a new vendor and healthcare data is in scope, procurement needs to see how discounts or committed-volume pricing will be reflected on invoices (line-level discounts vs a separate credit note). Is there a standard Redwood approach?

Can you confirm you can comply with the PO + Net 90 cadence or let us know what flexibility you have? If Net 90 is a hard constraint, please confirm we can get consolidated monthly statements with PO line references. Also share an invoice sample we will give to Accounts Payable.

Thanks,
Jane Smith

Subject: Re: HealthDocs procurement — PO details and invoice cadence

Hi Jane — really appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: we can put a PO number on every invoice, and we can supply both milestone-level invoices and consolidated monthly statements.

Couple of things to make billing operationally smooth and to keep the commercials fair for both sides:

- Invoice references: Redwood will include PO#, PO line item, and a short deliverable description on each invoice line as you requested.
- Net terms: Our standard is Net 60. If HealthDocs needs Net 90 we can accommodate but we typically ask for either a committed 12-month spend or a modest price offset to cover financing/cashflow. Practically we can offer:
  * Option A — Net 60, no changes to list pricing.
  * Option B — Net 90 on consolidated monthly invoices if HealthDocs signs a 12-month committed billing amendment (we can offer an 8% committed-volume discount).
  * Option C — Net 90 trial for the first 3 months, then revert to Net 60 unless a longer commit is agreed.

- Discounts: Redwood usually reflects discounts on the invoice as a line-level credit tied to the related service line. We can also issue a separate credit memo if you prefer one consolidated credit at month-end.

- Deliverables/milestone mapping: if you want milestone-specific invoicing, please share the PO line IDs you expect and we will map the SOW milestone IDs to them in our billing system.

I attached a short invoice template so AP can confirm it will pass their system (Invoice_template_sample.xlsx).

If Net 90 is non-negotiable for HealthDocs, Option B above tends to be the cleanest to get your terms while respecting Redwood’s cashflow. Happy to jump on a 20-minute call with you + finance to finalize. Sergio — looping you for commercial sign-off and to confirm discount cadence if HealthDocs leans into a 12-month commit. Neha — FYI on implementation mapping and how we handle milestone IDs in the invoice metadata.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Hi Olga / Jane,

Quick clarification from Finance: while Net 90 is our standard, there are a couple of practical guardrails we enforce that will affect how Redwood invoices us:

1) All invoices must include the PO number in the invoice header and each line item must reference the PO line code. Our AP system will reject invoices missing the PO line code.
2) If an invoice is a consolidated monthly statement we still require the mapping between statement lines and original PO-line IDs (so we can apply the right accounting codes).
3) If an invoice contains a line-level discount we prefer that to be shown as a separate credit line immediately below the affected service line (not buried in a separate attachment).

On flexibility: we can approve Option C (Net 90 trial / Net 60 afterwards) with procurement leadership sign-off, or we can accept Option B (Net 90 for 12-mo commit) provided you include an electronic amendment to the Master Services Agreement noting the commit and discount.

Two asks from our side to close fast:
- Please provide a redline to the SOW if any milestone IDs change (we try to keep SOW and PO in sync).
- Send a sample invoice (PDF) that shows PO#, PO line, and a credit line for the discount so our AP can pre-approve the format.

If you can send the sample by EOD Wednesday we should be able to issue a PO within 5 business days.

Tom Ellis
Director, Vendor Management | HealthDocs Inc.
Tom.Ellis@healthdocs.com
